newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland aims to be in EMU start group -PM Lipponen.
newsitem.headline: Finland aims to be in EMU start group -PM Lipponen.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Friday that Finland aimed to be among the countries joining the launch of the European Union's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) from the start in 1999.

"The EU will decide in spring 1998 on countries which will participate in the last stage of EMU from the beginning, on January 1, 1999. It is our aim to be among that group of countries," Lipponen said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery at Doshisha University in Japan.
A copy of the speech was distributed to the media here.
"It has been the stated policy of my government to make sure that Finland fulfils the so called convergence criteria which is a precondition for any (EU) member country," Lipponen said.

"And we have succeeded," he said, adding: "Being part of a European currency area would further strengthen Finland's position as a stable country to invest in." --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
